findings.namedBuyers: Kim Hussey is the currently published Manager of UHN Conference Services and the strongest named operational approach. Elisha Gacusan is explicitly named as the 2026 conference event contact by the Ontario Brain Injury Association; current 2027 responsibility is unverified. The 2027 event publishes UHN Conference Services, conferences@uhn.ca, rather than a named housing buyer. Neither person is verified as having hotel-contract signature authority.
findings.futureEdition: Confirmed upcoming edition: January 29, 2027, a one-day conference in Toronto, Ontario, Canada, within the requested horizon. The edition-specific landing, programme and venue pages consistently give this activity date. No officially announced 2028 edition was located. Annual recurrence does not establish a 2028 date. Data-quality exceptions: the 2027 registration page says registration closes January 26, 2026, while its footer gives January 29, 2027; the UHN overview lists October 7, 2026 beside the 19th conference. Neither inconsistent entry is adopted as the activity date.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel specifications: the 157-room Radisson Blu Toronto Downtown could accommodate a modest subset of visiting delegates, speakers or executives, but published attendance and overnight demand are unknown. This is a one-day hospital-site conference, so no extended-stay thesis is established. Its venue is not MTCC, making the hotel’s MTCC walking access less relevant. Harbourfront lodging would require a separate journey to Toronto Western Hospital. There is no basis to assume 15–109 peak rooms, full-hotel demand or an event-wide housing role. A leisure/resort rationale is unproven. Side meetings are a conditional future offer only; catering and restaurant availability must be checked before pitching food-and-beverage functions.
findings.venueCommitments: The published 2027 venue is BMO Education and Conference Centre, Toronto Western Hospital, 60 Leonard Avenue, Toronto, Ontario, Canada. This is in Toronto proper, at a hospital conference centre rather than a hotel; it is not the Harbourfront, MTCC or Exhibition Place site. Published venue selection is verified; the underlying venue contract was not reviewed.
findings.historicalRotation: Verified edition timeline: 17th, February 7, 2025 — Automotive Building (formerly Beanfield Centre), Exhibition Place, 105 Princes’ Boulevard, Toronto; 18th, January 30, 2026 — BMO Education and Conference Centre, Toronto Western Hospital; 19th, January 29, 2027 — same BMO centre. This establishes annual editions and a change of Toronto venue, not a multi-city rotation or an open future venue competition.
findings.accommodationSourcing: 2027 official instruction: “Participants should arrange their own accommodation. Please see below for a list of hotels in the area.” Every listed hotel: DoubleTree by Hilton, 108 Chestnut Street; The Chelsea, 33 Gerrard Street West; Marriott Downtown at CF Toronto Eaton Centre, 525 Bay Street; Hilton Toronto, 145 Richmond Street West; Courtyard by Marriott Toronto Downtown, 475 Yonge Street. These are suggestions, not published edition-specific room blocks or booking commitments. No official housing bureau, group rate, block size, open hotel RFP or peak-room/room-night figure was found for 2027. In contrast, 2025 explicitly reserved a Hotel X Toronto block for February 6, 2025 under “17th ABIC Conference,” at CAD335/night plus applicable taxes, with January 9, 2025 cutoff or earlier sellout; no block quantity is stated. That historical block is not current inventory.
findings.organizationStructure: Toronto Rehab hosts the conference; UHN Conference Services is the operating contact and UHN receives registration cheque payments. This is a healthcare-institution-led professional education conference, not an event owned by D.E. Systems or a verified independent association. D.E. Systems supplies the myConferenceSuite registration technology. No external PCO, DMC or housing bureau was identified on the reviewed edition pages.
findings.competitiveLimitations: Radisson Blu is absent from the 2027 suggested-hotel list. The five named alternatives have a visibility advantage, but the list is not evidence of exclusive allocations or committed lodging. No sellout, overflow requirement, hotel shortfall or displaced demand was found. Hotel X’s 2025 block demonstrates historical hotel procurement only, not a 2027 incumbent contract.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Approach Kim Hussey via kim.hussey@uhn.ca, copying conferences@uhn.ca, before preparing a room-block proposal. Ask who handles the 2027 conference, whether speakers or out-of-town delegates need lodging, whether accommodation-list inclusion is possible, and whether any unpublished hotel commitments exist. Ask for actual overnight participation and arrival/departure patterns rather than proposing a guessed block. Treat Elisha Gacusan as a historical referral only. For subsequent editions, seek an invitation to discuss lodging when plans are set; do not pitch replacement of the confirmed 2027 conference venue.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: 2027 conference-space capture is not an open opportunity: a venue is already published. Lodging is explicitly participant-arranged, so individual bookings may be commercially accessible, but organizer-controlled block demand, permission to join the accommodation list and a hotel-sourcing process remain unverified. Do not label hotel sourcing open or committed elsewhere.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Conditional relationship-development opportunity: ask whether a non-exclusive Harbourfront accommodation option or a small speaker/VIP allotment would be useful. The 2025 Hotel X block shows the series has used a hotel block before, while 2026 and 2027 direct participants to arrange accommodation themselves. This does not establish a future RFP, a rotating host-hotel requirement or 2028 room demand.
